original_question: Can motivic integration be generalized to Artin stacks in a way that is usable for McKay-correspondence-type results?
target_in_paper: Problem 10.3 in Section 10, read together with the immediately following discussion and nearby Problem 10.2: the paper asks to generalize motivic integration to Artin stacks, with the explicit nearby motivation that the theory should be relevant to McKay-correspondence-type applications beyond the Deligne-Mumford setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact mathematical object to be generalized (motivic integration) and the exact target category (Artin stacks), and it also captures the paper's nearby application filter, namely usefulness for McKay-correspondence-type results. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
missing_details: The paper's standing convention is that the base field is algebraically closed unless stated otherwise; that ambient hypothesis is implicit in the problem statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The problem is framed as extending the existing theory of motivic integration for (formal) Deligne-Mumford stacks, not as proposing an unrelated Artin-stack integration theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The intended use-case is the wild McKay correspondence beyond the Deligne-Mumford quotient-stack setting; the sentence after Problem 10.3 makes this application criterion explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

Nearby Problem 10.2 supplies the relevant scope: quotient stacks coming from more general groups/group schemes than the finite-group Deligne-Mumford case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
To match the paper's intent, the question should be posed as an open-ended development problem rather than merely a yes/no existence question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

No special variables, homogeneity conditions, degree restrictions, nilpotency assumptions, or asymptotic phrases such as 'for all sufficiently large m' occur in this problem; the omitted details are categorical and geometric, not numerical. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
refined_question: Can one develop a version of motivic integration for Artin stacks, extending the existing Deligne-Mumford-stack theory over the algebraically closed base field assumed in the paper, that is robust enough to formulate and prove wild McKay-correspondence-type statements for quotient stacks arising from more general groups/group schemes beyond the Deligne-Mumford setting? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 10 rather than any earlier conjecture or theorem: Problem 10.3 is the paper's exact Artin-stack generalization problem, and the sentence immediately after it explains why the draft's 'usable for McKay-correspondence-type results' clause is faithful rather than speculative. Nearby Problem 10.2 shows why Artin stacks are the natural next setting: the paper wants to extend the McKay correspondence to quotient stacks for more general groups/group schemes. The background theory being generalized is the Deligne-Mumford-stack formulation of the wild McKay correspondence in Section 2.3, especially the quotient-stack reformulation in equation (2.7). The only global hidden assumption needed to make the question stand alone is the paper-wide convention on the base field. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
